title: Style Profile Module — Style Extraction, Storage, and Prompt Injection
description: Create a style analysis module that extracts measurable writing patterns (sentence length, vocabulary richness, dialogue ratio, tense preference) from text samples, stores per-project style profiles, and injects style context into agent generation prompts. Register MCP endpoints /style/extract, /style/profile, /style/apply.
action: Create src-ts/src/agents/style-profile.ts with StyleExtractor and StyleProfileStore classes. Create src-ts/src/mcp/endpoints/style-profile.ts with POST /style/extract, GET /style/profile, POST /style/apply endpoints. StyleExtractor computes: avgSentenceLength, vocabRichness (unique/total ratio), dialogueRatio, tensePreference, avgParagraphLength, sentenceLengthDistribution (histogram). StyleProfileStore persists to projects/{id}/style-profile.json.
read_first: src-ts/src/agents/style-profile.ts (does not exist yet — create new)
desktop/src/services/workflowService.ts (reference: builtin-style-analysis workflow at lines 343-379, shows style extraction prompt pattern)
desktop/src/components/EvaluationPanel.tsx (reference: buildSuggestionActionTemplate function — where style context would be injected)

convergence.verification: Call /style/extract with sample text, verify StyleProfile output has all metrics. Store profile, retrieve via /style/profile, verify persistence. Call /style/apply and verify style_profile is included in prompt context.
convergence.definition_of_done: Style extraction produces measurable metrics from text, profiles persist per-project, and style context can be injected into generation prompts.

files.change: New file: StyleProfile interface, StyleExtractor class with extract(text) returning StyleProfile, StyleProfileStore with save/load methods
Unit tests: extraction metrics are correct for known text, profile save/load round-trip, vocab richness calculation
POST /style/extract, GET /style/profile/{projectId}, POST /style/apply (accepts text + style_profile, returns text with style guidance injected)

implementation: Define StyleProfile interface: { avgSentenceLength: number; vocabRichness: number; dialogueRatio: number; tensePreference: 'past'|'present'|'mixed'; avgParagraphLength: number; sentenceLengthDistribution: number[]; dominantPOV: 'first'|'third'|'mixed'; sampleHash: string; extractedAt: string }
Implement StyleExtractor.extract(text: string): StyleProfile — compute each metric using pure string analysis (no LLM needed for metrics, LLM only for POV detection)
avgSentenceLength = total words / sentence count (split on .!?；。！？)
vocabRichness = unique words / total words (after removing punctuation, case-insensitive)
dialogueRatio = dialogue sentences / total sentences (detect quoted speech: 「」""「」『』)
Implement StyleProfileStore.save(projectId, profile) and load(projectId) using fs read/write to projects/{id}/style-profile.json

Create MCP endpoints: /style/extract (accept text, return StyleProfile), /style/profile/{projectId} (GET, return stored profile), /style/apply (accept text + style_profile, return prompt context string with style instructions)
Write tests: known English text → verify sentence length, vocab richness. Known Chinese text → verify dialogue ratio. Profile save/load round-trip.

unit: style-profile.test.ts: Profile save and load round-trip

reference.pattern: builtin-style-analysis workflow in workflowService.ts uses LLM for style extraction — StyleExtractor adds deterministic metrics as a complement

rationale.chosen_approach: Deterministic metrics (no LLM) for reproducible, fast style analysis. LLM used only for qualitative aspects (POV detection). Stored profiles enable consistent style matching across sessions.
decision_factors: Deterministic metrics are reproducible and free
Analysis gap: style is extracted but never applied back
Style profiles must persist across sessions
rationale.tradeoffs: Deterministic metrics are less nuanced than LLM analysis, but are fast, free, and reproducible

risks: Style metrics may not capture all aspects of writing style — start with core metrics, extend later
